label: command-injection sources
old:
pattern-sources:
      - pattern-either:
          - pattern: request.query_params
          - pattern: request.path_params
          - pattern: (await request.json())
          - pattern: sys.argv
          - pattern: input(...)
    pattern-sinks:
      - patterns:
          - pattern-either:
              - pattern: os.system(...)
new:
pattern-sources:
      # sys.argv is NOT a source HERE, deliberately - same confused-deputy
      # argument as the path-traversal rule below. Whoever sets argv already
      # runs the process at its own privilege, so `tool --bin /usr/bin/x` is a
      # shell with extra steps, not an escalation. Measured against
      # cerberus/probes/ (29 .py driver scripts): argv -> subprocess.Popen fired
      # 5/5 and all 5 were false positives, each an operator naming the binary
      # they can already run. HTTP request data and stdin STAY: they cross a
      # trust boundary the argv supplier does not.
      - pattern-either:
          - pattern: request.query_params
          - pattern: request.path_params
          - pattern: (await request.json())
          - pattern: input(...)
    pattern-sinks:
      - patterns:
          - pattern-either:
              - pattern: os.system(...)
note: sys.argv is no longer a taint source for forge-taint-command-injection (confused deputy; 5/5 false positives on cerberus/probes)
